text:
alex: noticing a weird one — console sessions are occasionally showing rows from other workspaces after a fast workspace switch :thinking_face:
maria: ugh. repro steps?
alex: click org switcher -> choose workspace B within 200ms of opening A's page. sometimes B's saved searches list shows items from A
ryan: can you grab the network trace / cookies?
alex: attaching quick snippet from devtools: `GET /console/api/searches?ws=workspace-b`
alex: cookie header: `session=eyJhbGci...; workspace=workspace-a`
alex: server responded 200 with payload that contains items with `org_id: workspace-a`
kevin: that looks like header routing mismatch. maybe LB sticky session is routing request to pod that still has req-scoped context for ws A
maria: do we still use sticky-route by cookie? i thought we moved to header-based affinity last quarter
ryan: we do both, but affinity fallback exists: cookie -> header. if cookie present we prefer it for latency reasons
kevin: hmmm race condition: user changes workspace client-side, sets `workspace` cookie after sending header. request reaches a pod with old in-memory context keyed by cookie not header
alex: repro confirmed on my laptop. adding `workspace` cookie -> quick tab switch -> visible cross-rows ~30% of attempts
maria: severity? does this leak PII or just metadata?
alex: looks like resource ids + titles. could be sensitive depending on tenant data. high risk for dashboards showing private rows
ryan: immediate mitigation: make API ignore cookie workspace when `x-workspace` header present and different. prefer header over cookie for console API
kevin: agree. short term patch in gateway to reject cookie if header exists and mismatch, fall back to header. safer and small diff
maria: can we roll that out as a canary to 10% first? there are tenants that rely on cookie ordering maybe
ryan: yes, canary flag + circuit to log occurrences. also add metric `console.auth.workspace_mismatch`
alex: quick patch I tested locally: ```
if (req.headers['x-workspace'] && req.cookies.workspace && req.headers['x-workspace'] !== req.cookies.workspace) {
  // ignore cookie for routing
  req.cookies.workspace = req.headers['x-workspace'];
  metrics.inc('console.auth.workspace_mismatch');
}
```
kevin: that mutates cookie server-side — OK for routing but we should avoid persisting change back to client except when we want to sync. better to set routeKey = headerValue fallback cookieValue
ryan: good catch. alex please update to not override cookie. just use local var routeWorkspace = header || cookie
maria: timeline? if we push in next deploy window we can canary today and ramp tomorrow
alex: i'll open PR now. small change in api-gateway service (~8 LOC) + tests
kevin: also need a short-term console-client patch: when switching workspace, set `x-workspace` header on subsequent XHRs immediately before writing cookie, so header wins in race
ryan: client patch should be low-risk. add as canary too, but gateway fix first prevents leaks even from older clients
alex: i've seen one error path where server-side cache (LRU) stores last workspace result per session token. need to audit that cache keying — if it's keyed only by session id it will mix workspaces
kevin: omg. we did that for perf. cache key should include workspace id (header or cookie) and route variant. open a ticket to audit caches and add unit tests
nmaria: typo: n -> maria (sorry)
maria: agree on cache audit. for immediate response: 1) gateway header-over-cookie patch (canary 10%) 2) client header-first fix (canary) 3) add metric + alert if mismatch rate > 0.1% 4) audit caches 5) postmortem doc
ryan: i'll own the metric + alert + rollout playbook. kevin take the cache audit?
kevin: taking cache audit. alex submit PR for gateway and client stub
alex: PRs: #2356 (gateway), #2357 (console-client). broke tests locally but running CI now
deploy-bot: deploy queued — staging/gateway 09:12 UTC, staging/console-client 09:15 UTC :robot_face:
ryan: after staging pass, canary to 10% prod. I'll coordinate with SRE for burn-in window and rollback window (30m)
kevin: FYI this could interact with our rollouts UX: users who toggle workspace while rollout pinned to version X might see mismatched model of permissions. add note to rollout docs
maria: good call. we'll add a short blurb in Rollouts SOP about workspace-affinity hazards
alex: will follow up with minimal repro steps + screenshots in the PR description. thanks team :slightly_smiling_face:
kevin: big :eyes: on metrics after canary
ryan: tagging oncall: @kevin and @maria, please monitor
maria: on it
alex: will open postmortem draft once changes are live and we observe metric drop
kevin: estimated blast radius low but policy wise we treat as P0 until we confirm no sensitive leak remnants
ryan: agreed. keep channel updated
